title: Comparison of an optimized heart-lung machine setup with the conventional setup in patients with a body weight between 40 and 70 kg.
summary:
The heart-lung machine (HLM) is used as a form of extracorporeal circulation (EKZ) to maintain cardiovascular function during heart operations. One of the undesired side effects of using the HLM is hemodilution due to the filling volume of the single-use materials consisting of hoses, venous reservoir and the oxygenator (artificial lung). Attempts are already being made to keep this effect as low as possible by using hoses that are as short as possible and small disposable materials. When using the heart-lung machine in children's heart operations, disposable materials are used that are adapted to the respective weight of the children. In adults, however, disposable materials in only one size are used, regardless of body weight in a weight range from 40 kg to approx. 150 kg. A filling volume of approx. 1200 ml is usual. The filling volume leads to greater hemodilution, especially in adults with a lower body weight. The drop in the hemoglobin value caused by the haemodilution can cause organ damage and coagulation disorders and make it necessary to administer blood from another patient.
Based on these observations, the question arises as to whether it is advantageous for adults between 40 and 70 kg to use an optimized tubing set and thereby reduce hemodilution. Due to the lower drop in the Hb value to be expected at the HLM, an overall improved outcome of the patients is aimed for.
This does not affect the surgical procedure and there are no additional risks for the patient. Between September 2023 and February 2024, 70 adult patients with a body weight of 40 kg to 70 kg are to be included in the study and randomly divided into two groups (standard tubing set vs. optimized tubing set) who are planning heart surgery with HLM to be carried out at the Clinic for Cardiovascular Surgery at the University Hospital Freiburg.
conditions: Patients weighing between 40 and 70 kg who are undergoing heart surgery using a heart-lung machine

interventions.name: Use of a conventional heart-lung machine configuration in patients weighing between 40 and 70 kg
Use of an optimized configuration of the heart-lung machine in patients with a body weight between 40 and 70 kg

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Weight: 40 to 70 kg; Cardiac surgery with a heart-lung machine in normothermia
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency operations, operations in moderate hypothermia, endocarditis, reoperations, implantation of mechanical circulatory support devices, heart transplants, preoperative va-ECMO procedure
